Description
At TripleTen , we're building an international platform of digital re-skilling products to help people from diverse backgrounds learn new professions and build sustainable careers in tech.
Our program graduates have landed jobs at top companies like Tesla, Spotify, PlayStation, Google, and Microsoft. So far, over 5,000 students have chosen TripleTen, and hundreds of new students are joining us each month. We believe everyone can jumpstart a new career, which is why we produce quality educational content and offer intensive courses in tech complete with full access to an interactive platform, code reviews, and support from industry practitioners.
We're launching a program for experienced engineers transitioning into system architecture roles. The curriculum is being built by a team of senior authors. What we need now is the person who brings it to life for students: hosts the live sessions, reviews the work, runs the architecture review boards, and sets the technical bar for the people supporting alongside you.
This is a teaching and review role. You'll be the senior technical presence the cohort learns from week to week. You'll run live sessions and office hours, give real architectural feedback on student deliverables, and act as the escalation point for a team of supporting instructors who handle first-line questions.

The best person for this is someone who has actually designed and shipped systems at scale, has opinions about what good architecture looks like, and can tell an experienced engineer why their design is wrong, not just whether it runs.
Your audience: experienced engineers leveling up to system architecture roles. Many already write production code daily. They will spot shallow feedback instantly, so the bar here is real seniority, not familiarity.
Format: Async-first with scheduled live sessions. Live sessions and office hours are timed around a US-based cohort. Estimated 15 to 25 hrs/week.
Please submit all resumes or CV's in English.

Host weekly live sessions across the program, focused on the design and decision layer: where to split services, how systems scale and fail, which tradeoff to make and why
Run group office hours and 1:1 sessions for students working through projects and the capstone
Review student projects against rubrics: the architecture dossiers, deployed backends, cloud infrastructure, performance reports, security reviews, and the final distributed-system capstone
Give architectural feedback, not just pass/fail checks. Catch when a design decision is unsound, an interface is wrong, or a scope is unrealistic, and explain the better path
Run the mock architecture review boards and the simulated executive-panel presentations, and give structured, senior-level critique
Set the technical standard for a team of supporting instructors who cover questions and first-line review, and act as their escalation point on design and architecture calls

5+ years as a senior software/systems architect, platform engineer, or senior backend/infrastructure engineer
Has designed and shipped systems at scale in a real company, not just coursework or side projects
Depth across the architectural spine: system design, API and service architecture, cloud and infrastructure (AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD), and distributed systems
Can explain why a decision was made, not just how it was implemented, and can diagnose and critique someone else's architecture live
Strong technical communication: comfortable leading a live session and writing clear, specific review feedback
Strong English C1+ — instruction and review are in English for a US-based audience
Comfortable using AI tools in day-to-day technical work
What we can offer you
Milestone-based payments tied to deliverables
Fully remote work with flexible hours
A digital office — we use modern tools (Notion, Miro, Slack, Figma) to keep collaboration smooth
Professional trust and autonomy — no micromanaging
The chance to see real impact: our metric is graduates landing jobs in tech
Join a diverse, international, and close-knit team excited to work with you

Job Summary: The Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) provides operations support services and business solutions to the community of 10,000 House Members, Officers and staff.

The CAO organization comprises more than 800 technical and administrative staff working in a variety of areas, including information technology, finance, budget management, human resources, payroll, child care, food and vending, procurement, logistics and administrative counsel.

This position is located in the Network Engineering and Operations (Networking) Directorate, House Information Resources (HIR), Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), U.S. House of Representatives (House).

The Networking Directorate provides operational support services to the House that ensure reliable and dependable connectivity to the House Data Network both on the House Campus and to over 820 District Offices as well as numerous Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) sites, facilities, and mobile capabilities.

This position does not have day-today supervisory/managerial responsibilities. Primary Responsibilities: Evaluates and recommends commercially available, standards compliant LAN networking solutions.

Design, test, and implement new LAN deployments and upgrades based on project requirements Designs complex integrated communication networks and develops network service specifications and procedures. Provides operational support on day‐to‐day operations and resolution to complex LAN, WAN, Wireless and ISE related problems.

Assists in the preparation of Request for Proposals and Request for Quotations. Reviews and evaluates reliable, cost‐effective, and efficient campus LAN communications for the House. Conducts performance and bandwidth utilization monitoring of LAN communication systems.

Keeps abreast of relevant routing and switching technology changes and applies industry standards to House requirements. Trains other House staff in telecommunications technologies and provides technical guidance to junior level engineers. Performs other official duties and special projects as assigned.
Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent work experience. Minimum 5 years of experience designing and supporting large scale campus LAN/ WAN and wireless networks. Knowledge of TCP, UDP, QoS, SNMP, TLS/HTTPS, SMTP, EIGRP, OSPF, and BGP.

Experience with Aruba wireless access hardware ideal but not required. Demonstrate proficiency with managing large scale enterprise networks using Cisco’s routing and switching best practices.

Strong understanding of how to configure access ports and trunk ports Knowledge of port security and how to define violation modes on layer 2 access points Proficient in using design tools such as Visio to road map the enterprise infrastructure. Skill in the coordination of network engineering and integration projects.

Knowledge, Skill, and Ability (KSA) and Competency Requirements: Ability to provide engineering leadership on all phases of analysis, design, testing, and implementation of networks, integration of voice and data, and telecommunications.

Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with elected officials, senior staff, information systems professional, and non-technical users.

Employees within this position are expected to demonstrate the following IHR Technical Competencies: Analytics; Application Administration and Integration; Emergency Response Planning and Risk Management; Hardware Installation and Management; Information Management; Information Resources Strategy and Planning; Information Systems/Network Security; Information Technology Support; Knowledge of Emerging Trends and Industry Best Practices; Network Management; Project Management; Quality Assurance and Testing; and Telecommunications.

All employees within CAO are expected to demonstrate the following general competencies: Accountability, Adaptability, Collaboration, Communication, Customer Orientation, Knowledge of Relevant Policies, Procedures, and Processes, Priority Management, and Problem Resolution. Certifications: CCNA or CCNP preferred.

Continued employment is contingent upon satisfactorily completing a criminal history records check (or other applicable security clearance) and a pre-employment drug-test (pre-identified position only).

Ihre Karriere in der Entwicklung zukunftsweisender Lösungen für die Elektromobilität.
Mit BRÜGGEN ENGINEERING gestalten Sie das funktionale Verhalten moderner Hochvolt-Inverter und elektrifizierter Antriebe. Sie entwickeln und validieren anspruchsvolle Funktionen, lösen technische Fragestellungen auf Gesamtfahrzeugebene und übernehmen die fachliche Abstimmung mit Kunden sowie internationalen Entwicklungsteams.
Aufgaben
Funktionsentwicklung: Sie verantworten die Entwicklung und Absicherung von Funktionen für Hochvolt-Inverter und elektrische Antriebssysteme über den gesamten Produktlebenszyklus.
Antriebskonzepte: Sie erarbeiten funktionale Konzepte und Anforderungen für Motorregelung, Leistungselektronik und elektrischen Fahrzeugantrieb.
Systemintegration: Sie koordinieren die Umsetzung der Funktionen in Zusammenarbeit mit Softwareentwicklung, Kalibrierung, Hardware, Test und funktionaler Sicherheit.
Erprobung: Sie begleiten Integrations- und Fahrzeugtests, bewerten das Systemverhalten und leiten notwendige Optimierungen ab.
Problemlösung: Sie analysieren funktionale Abweichungen und Fehlerbilder und entwickeln nachhaltige Lösungen unter Berücksichtigung des Gesamtantriebs.
Kundenabstimmung: Sie vertreten die verantworteten Funktionen in technischen Gesprächen und stimmen Anforderungen, Ergebnisse und offene Punkte direkt mit dem Kunden ab.
Technische Steuerung: Sie bewerten Risiken, berichten über den Entwicklungsstatus und führen komplexe Themen fachlich bis zum erfolgreichen Abschluss.
Qualifikation
Qualifikation: Abgeschlossenes Masterstudium in Fahrzeugtechnik, Elektrotechnik, Elektronik, Mechatronik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung
Erfahrung: Mindestens zehn Jahre Berufserfahrung in der automobilen System- oder Funktionsentwicklung, vorzugsweise im Bereich Hochvolt-Inverter, Leistungselektronik oder elektrifizierte Antriebe
Antriebstechnik: Fundierte Kenntnisse in Inverterfunktionen, Motorregelungsverfahren und elektrischen Antriebssystemen
Systementwicklung: Erfahrung in Anforderungsmanagement, Funktionsarchitektur, Integration sowie Verifikation und Validierung
Problemlösung: Ausgeprägte Fähigkeiten im Trouble-Shooting, in der Root-Cause-Analyse und bei der Bewertung komplexer Systemzusammenhänge
Sicherheit: Kenntnisse der funktionalen Sicherheit nach ISO 26262 und der Anforderungen an Hochvoltsysteme
Tools: Erfahrung mit Polarion, JIRA, Enterprise Architect sowie MATLAB und Simulink von Vorteil
Kommunikation: Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse, Deutschkenntnisse von Vorteil, sowie Reisebereitschaft nach Luxemburg von bis zu 25 %

Attraktive Konditionen: Unbefristete Vollzeitstelle mit einer Vergütung, die Ihrer Qualifikation und Erfahrung entspricht
Zukunftssichere Projekte: Gestalten Sie innovative Antriebsfunktionen für hybride und vollelektrische Fahrzeuge
Dynamisches Team: Werden Sie Teil eines internationalen Entwicklungsumfelds, das technische Verantwortung und interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit fördert
Wir freuen uns auf Ihre aussagekräftigen Bewerbungsunterlagen mit
Angabe Ihres frühesten Starttermins und Ihrer Gehaltsvorstellung.

Job Summary We are seeking a Storage Engineer with deep expertise across enterprise storage platforms — NetApp ONTAP, Pure Storage, and Ceph — to design, deploy, and operate the storage foundation that supports our compute, virtualization, database, and Kubernetes workloads.

The role spans block, file, and object storage across data center, edge, and cloud environments, with strong attention to performance, data protection, and cost.

The ideal candidate has operated heterogeneous storage estates at scale, understands the storage characteristics of diverse workloads, and brings strong automation discipline to storage engineering work. Key Responsibilities Design and operate enterprise storage platforms across NetApp ONTAP, Pure Storage FlashArray/FlashBlade, and Ceph.

Implement and manage SAN, NAS, and object storage across data center and cloud environments. Build storage solutions for VMware, Kubernetes (CSI drivers), and database workloads. Design and operate replication, snapshot, and backup strategies for critical data assets.

Implement and operate cloud-tiered storage with FabricPool, CloudVolumes, or equivalent. Build storage automation using Ansible, Terraform, REST APIs, and platform-native automation. Operate Ceph clusters including OSD lifecycle, CRUSH maps, RGW, RBD, and CephFS.

Design and operate storage performance management for high-throughput and latency-sensitive workloads. Implement data protection strategies including ransomware protection and immutable snapshots.

Build storage observability across capacity, performance, and health dimensions, surfacing the signals operators need to spot capacity pressure, performance regressions, and failing components before users feel the impact.

Lead storage upgrades, firmware lifecycle management, and security patching across the storage estate, planning each campaign to maintain availability for the workloads dependent on the platform. Drive storage cost optimization including deduplication, compression, and tiering strategies.

Troubleshoot complex storage issues spanning array, network, and host layers. Stay current with storage industry developments and emerging platforms, regularly review release notes and community discussions, and translate noteworthy advances into concrete recommendations and adoption proposals for the team.

Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field. Five or more years of enterprise storage engineering experience. Deep expertise in NetApp ONTAP or Pure Storage FlashArray/FlashBlade. Hands-on experience with Ceph at production scale.

Strong understanding of SAN, NAS, and object storage protocols. Experience with storage integration for VMware and Kubernetes (CSI). Strong scripting and automation skills using Ansible, Terraform, or REST APIs. Strong understanding of storage performance, capacity planning, and cost optimization.

Strong troubleshooting skills across storage, network, and host layers. Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Preferred Qualifications Vendor certifications (NCDA, NCIE, Pure Storage certifications). Experience with hybrid-cloud storage replication. Job Summary We are seeking an experienced Semiconductor Software Engineer to design and build software tooling, firmware, and infrastructure that support semiconductor design, verification, manufacturing, and post-silicon validation.

In this role you will partner with hardware engineers and EDA teams to build software that accelerates silicon development cycles and improves yield, performance, and quality.

The ideal candidate will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with practical experience working alongside hardware teams in EDA, verification, or post-silicon environments.

In this role you will work closely with cross-functional partners — product, design, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders — to translate ambiguous requirements into well-engineered solutions, and will be expected to raise the bar through code review, design review, and mentorship of more junior engineers.

The successful candidate brings strong engineering discipline, a clear communication style, and a track record of shipping meaningful work that holds up well in production. Key Responsibilities Design and build software tooling that accelerates semiconductor design and verification workflows.

Develop firmware and low-level software interacting directly with silicon, including drivers and BSPs. Build infrastructure to support large-scale EDA tool execution on compute farms and cloud platforms.

Develop post-silicon validation tooling, including high-throughput test orchestration, programmable stimulus generation, and result aggregation systems that scale across many parts and many test environments. Build data pipelines for design, verification, and characterization data, supporting downstream analytics and ML.

Implement debug tooling and diagnostic infrastructure for hardware bring-up and silicon characterization, giving engineers fast feedback loops on the silicon-software interface during critical validation windows. Partner with hardware engineers to translate hardware-specific requirements into clean software designs.

Optimize software for performance and scalability in compute-intensive semiconductor workflows. Lead architecture and code reviews that span the software-hardware boundary, ensuring that abstractions, interfaces, and constraints between the two domains are well-understood and respected across the team.

Contribute to internal libraries and tooling shared across silicon design teams.

Maintain comprehensive, current technical documentation — including architecture diagrams, design decisions, configuration references, runbooks, and operational procedures — so that the system remains supportable, auditable, and easy to onboard new engineers onto over time.

Mentor and coach junior and mid-level engineers through code review, design review, pair programming, and structured knowledge sharing, helping the broader team grow in technical maturity and confidence over time.

Continuously evaluate emerging hardware platforms and toolchains, assessing maturity, fit for purpose, and total cost of ownership, and make grounded recommendations on which to adopt, pilot, or defer based on real engineering needs.

Required Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Six or more years of software engineering experience, with significant time in semiconductor environments. Strong programming skills in C, C++, and Python.

Hands-on experience with EDA, verification, or post-silicon validation workflows. Solid understanding of hardware-software interaction at a low level. Experience building large-scale compute infrastructure (grid, cloud, HPC). Strong scripting and automation skills. Experience with data pipelines for design or characterization data.

Excellent debugging and troubleshooting skills. Strong communication and documentation skills. Preferred Qualifications Exposure to SystemVerilog or other HDLs. Familiarity with UVM-based verification workflows. Experience with cloud-based EDA workflows. Hands-on experience with ML applied to silicon design. Advanced degree in EE or related field.

Building AI-powered tools and agents. You will integrate applied AI into our workflows using modern frameworks. You will consult with business stakeholders to help explain the art of the possible, guide them in defining logic and prompts, and own building and maintaining agentic workflows and tools.

Example projects include building an AI-powered QA and training tool with a RAG component for new support agents, architecting agentic workflows for our onboarding team, or building a FreshDesk integration that suggests draft responses to tickets.

Building and maintaining a shared agent platform. This is what makes AI scale beyond our team. You will build and maintain the templates, approved patterns, and deployment infrastructure that enable people across Customer Operations to build their own agents without needing to figure out hosting, monitoring, or API connectivity themselves.

When a Technical Services lead wants to build an agent that automates "pixel not firing" investigations, they should be able to do it on your platform without writing a deployment script. You own making self-serve actually work.

Building robust internal software, integrations, and automations - such as developing custom FreshDesk widgets to support our agents. You will own the full lifecycle of these apps: building, hosting, monitoring, maintaining, and eventually retiring them when they're no longer needed.
Many job descriptions define themselves as "critical" or "pivotal." This role genuinely is. impact.com has thousands of clients, millions of partners, endless data, and complex multi-system processes. As a business, we are ensuring we are on the cutting edge - aggressively automating and scaling up what we do with AI.

This role owns a substantial portion of that transformation for a critical part of our business. A note on how you'll work with others: when someone across Customer Operations builds a pilot that proves value, you don't take it over.

You partner with them to elevate it - bringing engineering rigor, production infrastructure, and scale while they maintain creative control and ongoing input. When someone has a great idea but isn't technical enough to build it themselves, your first instinct is to build it with them, growing their skills in the process.

You're an accelerator, not a bottleneck. This role is for the person who embodies the overlap of curiosity, process-obsession, and action orientation. It is for the passionate tinkerer who also gets carried away exploring custom Salesforce structures and data flows.

It is for the person who has been building agentic workflows to manage their household tasks in their free time because they can't stop playing with the new tools AI offers. Software Development Foundation: Proven experience building, hosting, and maintaining applications and tools. API & Integration Expertise: Deep experience working with REST APIs. You can easily build connectors between distinct SaaS platforms to automate data flows and trigger actions.

Systems Thinking & Process Orientation: You don't write code in a vacuum; you map out complex operational workflows before you start building. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work closely with non-technical business stakeholders. You can take a process flow and prompt designs from a business leader and turn them into a functioning, hosted application. Equally important: you can teach - walking a non-technical person through building their first agent is as valuable as building it yourself.

Autonomous Builder: You are a self-starter who thrives in an agile environment. You don't need excessive hand-holding to figure out how to host a script or deploy a small internal app.

Where Europe's enterprises adopt AI
Langdock is the AI platform used by more than 10,000 companies to give employees secure access to the leading AI models, to build and share agents and to automate repetitive workflows. We have grown past $40M ARR while remaining a small team, and we care deeply about operating efficiently across the entire company.
For many enterprises, Langdock is becoming the place where most of the net-new work is produced. As people and agents create more documents, analyses, decisions, and automations inside AI interfaces, the context and data behind that work accumulate within Langdock. This gives us the opportunity to earn a larger role in their technology stack by building a platform they choose to rely on.
Our ambition is to build that platform for European enterprises while preserving their control over data, model providers, and deployment environments. We have made meaningful progress at the application layer, but much of the foundation beneath it still needs to be built.
You can watch the Meet the engineering team video to get a feeling for how we work.

Systems Engineers solve our most complex technical problems inside and across Langdock's shared services when existing building blocks or standard architectures are insufficient. These are problems where correctness under failure, performance, scale, security, and cost interact.
This is a project-oriented role rather than ownership of one permanent layer. You might spend a period on distributed execution, then move into storage architecture, workload isolation, or model serving as company priorities change. The constant is sustained investigation of unfamiliar systems and responsibility for turning that understanding into a production system.
Systems Engineers own the difficult mechanism and the measurable improvement it creates, whether in correctness, capability, performance, reliability, or cost. They operate what they build, while the Platform owner remains accountable for the service contract and long-term lifecycle around it.
What you might work on

Distributed state and execution. Design systems that remain correct when work is concurrent, long-running, retried, resumed, or moved between processes. Define explicit invariants for ordering, idempotency, recovery, and tenant isolation.
Storage and data systems. Improve how large volumes of customer and agent-generated data are stored, versioned, moved, and recovered while preserving consistency, data residency, and predictable performance.
Secure compute for agents. Develop the isolation, runtime, and scheduling mechanisms behind a shared sandbox service for untrusted code. The system needs persistent filesystems, deny-by-default networking, scoped mounts, fast startup, suspension, resumption, and predictable scheduling without weakening the security boundary.
Inference systems. Improve the serving systems beneath the Model Gateway, optimizing throughput, latency, accelerator utilization, reliability, and cost. The work is measurement driven: understand the workload, identify the actual bottleneck, and decide where changes to serving, scheduling, caching, model format, or hardware create structural advantage.
Resource scheduling and isolation. Make CPU, memory, storage, network, and accelerator capacity explicit so one workload cannot degrade another. Improve placement, admission control, backpressure, autoscaling, and recovery across deployment environments.
Billing and usage metering. Build the concurrent metering mechanism behind the billing capability, accounting for heterogeneous units such as model tokens and sandbox compute time. It must stay correct when many workloads report concurrently, events arrive late or more than once, and long-running jobs reserve capacity before their final usage is known. This involves idempotent ingestion, atomic reservations, reconciliation, and auditable records.
You will start with one focused problem based on your experience and the team's priorities. The expectation is not broad activity across every domain; it is a substantial improvement in the capability, performance, reliability, or economics of the system you take on.
Tech stack
Go and TypeScript in one Bazel monorepo, with implementation choices driven by the system
Linux, containers, microVMs, filesystems, and networking
Protobuf and gRPC for service contracts
Kubernetes across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on-premises deployments
Terraform and Terragrunt for infrastructure orchestration
PostgreSQL and Redis where durable metadata or coordination requires them
Open-source model serving and accelerator infrastructure
You do not need prior experience with every item. You do need enough systems depth to enter an unfamiliar part of the stack, understand its behavior, and make consequential changes safely.
How we work
We operate with high trust and autonomy in squads of 3 to 4 engineers. A squad owns its roadmap, prioritization, technical decisions, and operation in production. Engineers are expected to find the context they need, ask for input when it improves the outcome, and move work forward without waiting for every next step to be assigned.
We align asynchronously before scheduling a meeting. Product requirement documents (PRDs) define the user problem, intended outcome, and constraints. Design documents make architectural boundaries, tradeoffs, failure modes, migrations, and rollouts explicit. People read and challenge the thinking asynchronously; once the context is shared, a short in-office discussion or whiteboard session usually resolves the remaining questions quickly.
We optimize for leverage. Engineers choose the AI tools that work for them, supported by clear ticket context, focused branches, automated tests, and AI review before human review. We also invest in observability, migration tooling, automated recovery, and runbooks so recurring product maintenance does not depend on someone remembering a manual step.
The engineer who ships a change owns it in production. If something breaks, you lead the fix.

You have owned technically difficult production systems in areas such as distributed systems, databases, runtimes, inference, networking, or storage. You operate what you build and remain responsible for it after deployment.
You reason from first principles, form testable hypotheses, and use measurement to understand unfamiliar behavior. You investigate beyond the first working solution until you understand the underlying mechanism.
Given an underspecified problem, you identify the most important invariant, decide where depth will change the outcome, and defend what you deliberately leave out.
You reason precisely about concurrency, isolation, ordering, data loss, and failure, while finding pragmatic ways to improve performance, reliability, or cost without unnecessary complexity.
You use AI tools as leverage while verifying their output and retaining ownership of the result. You communicate complex systems clearly, expose uncertainty, and work constructively with others.

# Ingénieur Système Senior Kubernetes & Linux #
## Qui a besoin de votre renfort ? ##
Votre nouveau défi se trouve chez EveryWare, le principal fournisseur suisse de services Cloud et IT avec une infrastructure DataCenter et réseau hautement évolutive à Zurich - et spécialisé dans les besoins des clients professionnels.

Fort de plus de 20 ans d'expertise, l'entreprise conçoit et exploite des architectures Cloud privées, publiques et hybrides, ainsi que des plateformes d'hébergement et IT managées. Environ 250 collaborateurs, dont 90 % d'ingénieurs spécialisés, apportent des innovations internationales applicables aux entreprises suisses.

Plus de 3000 entreprises ainsi que 30 partenaires commerciaux ont déjà choisi EveryWare comme partenaire. Plus de 200 grands projets réussis pour des clients professionnels, y compris des clients des secteurs bancaire et assurantiel, témoignent de la compétence d'EveryWare.
## Comment vous créez de la valeur ##
Vous ne voulez pas seulement maintenir les systèmes en fonctionnement, mais construire vous-même la plateforme derrière ? Dans l'équipe Alpha, vous prenez la tête de la construction de nouvelles plateformes Kubernetes - y compris la pipeline de déploiement. Ce n'est pas un environnement prêt à l'emploi où l'on vous attribue une partie : ici, quelque chose de nouveau est créé, et vous êtes celui qui le construit.
En parallèle, vous êtes responsable avec vos collègues de l'infrastructure de nos clients Managed-Service issus du secteur bancaire et assurantiel. Tout fonctionne sur site dans notre propre Cloud privé - nous ne louons pas chez un hyperscaler, nous construisons nous-mêmes. L'équipe est petite et les chemins sont courts : si vous avez une bonne idée et pouvez la justifier, vous la mettez en œuvre.

* Vous construisez notre nouvelle plateforme Kubernetes, l'exploitez et l'étendez pour de nouveaux projets clients.
* Vous planifiez et gérez les déploiements CI/CD et faites avancer l'automatisation au sein de l'équipe.
* Vous dirigez techniquement les projets clients et internes - de la planification à la mise en œuvre dans les délais.
* Vous gérez notre infrastructure IdM et API Management.
* Vous prenez en charge avec vos collègues l'exploitation et le développement de nos serveurs Linux, Unix et FreeBSD ainsi que des bases de données basées sur Linux (PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, DB2). L'environnement existant restera en place encore quelques années - vous devez le connaître, mais votre focus est ailleurs.
* Vous assurez le support de second et troisième niveau pour nos clients et analysez les incidents complexes jusqu'à leur cause.
* Vous participez au service de garde : rotation de 5, soit une semaine toutes les cinq semaines. Les interventions de nuit sont rares, et vous n'êtes jamais seul.
## Ce qui vous distingue ##
Une chose est vraiment importante pour nous, le reste est accessoire : vous avez exploité Kubernetes en production pendant plusieurs années. Pas dans un homelab et pas "avoir déjà démarré un conteneur", mais avoir déployé et géré des environnements plus vastes. Le background Linux en découle naturellement.
À cela s'ajoute une attitude qui nous convient : vous vous organisez vous-même, aimez prendre des décisions et vous plongez dans des systèmes inconnus sans attendre une documentation prête.

* Expérience de plusieurs années dans l'exploitation productive de Kubernetes, idéalement incluant Rancher.
* Solide expérience Linux en tant qu'ingénieur système, de préférence chez un prestataire IT ou un hébergeur.
* Expérience avec CI/CD et automatisation (Gitea, GitLab, GitLab Runner, Jenkins, Harbor, Ansible, etc.) ainsi que scripting sûr (Shell, Python).
* Compréhension de base des réseaux (TCP/IP) - vous n'avez pas besoin de configurer des firewalls, mais de comprendre ce qui se passe sur le réseau.
* Vous n'êtes pas un linuxien dogmatique : chez nous, Windows est aussi présent dans l'environnement.
* Vous avez l'envie de vous développer - ceux qui croient tout savoir s'ennuient chez nous.
* Très bon allemand, vous comprenez le suisse allemand. Anglais courant - vous devez aussi argumenter avec nos partenaires, pas seulement communiquer.
* Résidence à proximité : pour le service de garde, une heure maximum pour être physiquement présent dans le centre de données.
Ce que vous n'avez pas besoin d'apporter : Solaris, AIX ou des certifications. Nous évaluons votre façon de penser lors d'un entretien basé sur un cas concret - pas sur du papier.
Atouts : expérience dans le secteur bancaire ou assurantiel, gestion d'identité (Authentik, FreeIPA).
## Avantages ##
### Emplacement TOP ###
Votre nouveau lieu de travail se trouve dans un bâtiment unique avec beaucoup de charme - au cœur de Zurich. Transports publics et innombrables possibilités de déjeuner sont accessibles à pied.
### Projets exigeants ###
Notre expertise en conception, construction et exploitation de plateformes de pointe avec les technologies Cloud les plus modernes se reflète dans plus de 200 grands projets réussis.
### Savoir-faire concentré ###
La passion technique rencontre une expertise approfondie. Ici, vous bénéficiez d'une riche expérience et d'un réseau hautement professionnel.
### Formation continue ###
Vous trouverez chez nous un environnement de travail qui s'adapte en permanence aux exigences du marché et des clients. De nombreuses possibilités de formation internes et externes vous attendent donc.
### Stabilité & croissance ###
En tant qu'entreprise suisse avec plus de 20 ans d'histoire à succès, nous misons sur la stabilité, la confiance et des relations à long terme - avec les clients et les collaborateurs.
### Intégration structurée ###
Un programme d'intégration structuré avec des mentors personnels vous permet un démarrage sans accroc.

s.h: Ce qui rend ton quotidien passionnant
s.t:
Installer et utiliser Windows, ça prend quelques minutes. La mise en place d'un logiciel de gestion est déjà plus complexe. Tu aides les PME suisses à adapter le logiciel Abacus à leurs besoins et à leurs processus.
Après une introduction soignée et personnalisée, tu prends la responsabilité de « ton » projet ou mandat client. Tu peux alors compter sur le soutien de tes collègues.
Avec les clients, tu analyses leurs processus, tu recueilles leurs besoins et tu les documentes.
Tu mets ensuite en place la solution logicielle sur mesure chez le client. Cela dure généralement plusieurs semaines et tu travailles souvent directement sur quoi enrichir encore ton quotidien.
Ton portefeuille de tâches comprend également l'organisation et l'animation d'ateliers et de formations pour les utilisateurs de tes clients.

Tu n'as pas forcément besoin d'être déjà un pro du logiciel, mais un grand intérêt pour l'informatique est aussi important que la fascination pour la digitalisation et les opportunités qu'elle offre pour l'optimisation des processus.
Tu saisis rapidement les liens entre les choses, tu aimes apprendre de nouvelles choses et l'ambition te gagne dès qu'il s'agit de comprendre le métier de tes clients et de leur proposer de bonnes solutions.
Ce que nous imaginons dans ton bagage de formation ? Pas si simple, car de nombreux chemins mènent jusqu'à nous. Une formation commerciale ou technique complétée par un perfectionnement en gestion d'entreprise de niveau HES/ES ou par un brevet fédéral a de bonnes chances d'aboutir, que ce soit déjà terminé ou en passe de l'être.
Des connaissances de base en anglais et/ou en allemand sont idéalement nécessaires pour évoluer aisément dans notre environnement.
Si tu as déjà été en contact avec Abacus ou d'autres systèmes ERP, tant mieux. Peut\-être au service commercial interne. Ou dans la gestion des stocks. Ou dans un service financier. Mais ce n'est pas une condition.
Tes futurs collègues attendent avec impatience le renfort d'une personne simple et sympa, qui aime rire, y compris d'elle\-même. Et oui, il y a du pain sur la planche : il faudra savoir « foncer tête baissée ». Ça vaut le coup, promis.

s.h: Et voici ce que tu y gagnes
s.t:
Un poste exigeant mais passionnant, dans lequel nous te formons soigneusement sur place. Et une fois à l'aise, de très belles perspectives d'évolution.
Cela nous gêne un peu de nous vanter d'avoir sans doute le meilleur esprit d'équipe à des kilomètres à la ronde. C'est pourquoi nous citons simplement un avis cinq étoiles de Kununu : « L'esprit d'équipe est une valeur essentielle ». Et c'est vrai !
De zéro à cent en 15… non, pas secondes, années. Nous avons grandi vite, mais sainement, et nous sommes bien organisés. Pourtant, une chose n'a pas changé depuis nos débuts : nos structures restent légères et tu trouves facilement le bon interlocuteur.
Dans notre domaine, nous comptons parmi les grands acteurs et sommes reconnus pour notre grande qualité. Rien d'étonnant à ce que nous soyons régulièrement distingués comme partenaire d’intégration exceptionnel.
Un bon salaire, que tu peux influencer par tes performances. Assurance perte de gain maladie et assurance accidents ? Nous les prenons en charge. Avec les autres avantages, cela représente vite plusieurs milliers de francs par an.
Nous aurions encore tellement à raconter. Ce qui rend ton job chez nous passionnant, par exemple. Qui nous sommes et comment nous fonctionnons. Alors n'hésite pas et fais\-toi ta propre idée.
Déjà convaincu(e) ? Tu préférerais commencer aujourd’hui plutôt que demain ? Alors envoie\-nous ton CV ou le lien vers ton profil LinkedIn. Au Laboratoire d'Ingénierie de la Réhabilitation (RELab) de l'ETH Zurich, nous développons ax|ReCover, une plateforme modulaire de réhabilitation basée sur smartphone qui vise à transformer les smartphones du quotidien en dispositifs de thérapie intelligents pour les personnes souffrant de déficiences des membres supérieurs suite à des blessures neurologiques ou traumatiques.

Notre solution unique combine matériel modulaire, électronique embarquée, capteurs physiologiques et biomécaniques, ainsi que logiciel mobile pour rendre la réhabilitation plus accessible, engageante et personnalisée. Nous recherchons un nouveau membre d'équipe souhaitant développer des produits qui améliorent directement la vie des personnes.
## Contexte du projet ##
Dans le cadre d'un projet financé par Innosuisse, nous recherchons un ingénieur systèmes embarqués avec une solide expérience en électronique pour diriger le développement et l'amélioration de la plateforme de détection embarquée d'ax|ReCover.

Le financement pour ce poste spécifique est limité à 16 mois et lié à des lots de travail spécifiques dans ce projet Innosuisse.

En collaboration étroite avec notre équipe de recherche, vous serez responsable du firmware embarqué et de l'électronique qui alimentent notre système modulaire de réhabilitation, avec pour objectif de transformer des prototypes de recherche en un produit robuste et manufacturable.

Il s'agit d'un rôle très pratique couvrant le logiciel embarqué, l'électronique, les capteurs, le prototypage et le développement produit, dans le domaine des technologies de neuro-réhabilitation.
## Description du poste ##
* Développer le firmware embarqué pour notre plateforme modulaire de réhabilitation ax|ReCover.
* Concevoir, implémenter et valider des pipelines fiables d'acquisition de capteurs
* Intégrer des capteurs biomécaniques et physiologiques dans des systèmes embarqués
* Développer la communication Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) entre ax|ReCover et le smartphone
* Mettre en œuvre une acquisition synchronisée des capteurs et un streaming de données
* Concevoir et itérer des schémas électroniques et des PCB pour de nouvelles révisions matérielles
* Sélectionner les composants électroniques et contribuer aux décisions d'architecture électronique
* Mettre en service et valider des PCB personnalisés
* Développer des pilotes bas niveau pour les capteurs et les périphériques de communication
* Collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe de recherche sur l'intégration électronique et le développement de prototypes
* Utiliser des oscilloscopes, analyseurs logiques, multimètres et autres équipements de laboratoire pour diagnostiquer les problèmes matériels et firmware
* Optimiser la consommation d'énergie, la fiabilité de la communication et la performance du système embarqué
* Soutenir les tests électroniques, la validation et la vérification de conception
* Aider à établir des processus d'ingénierie et de documentation pour le développement réglementaire futur
## Profil ##
* Un MSc ou BSc en génie électrique, systèmes embarqués, génie informatique, robotique ou discipline apparentée
* Solides compétences en programmation C/C++
* Expérience dans le développement et le test de firmware pour microcontrôleurs ARM Cortex-M ou similaires
* Expérience avec Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
* Expérience avec SPI, I²C, UART, ADC, DMA, interruptions et timers
* Expérience dans la conception ou l'itération d'électronique embarquée personnalisée, y compris la capture de schémas et la conception de PCB avec KiCad, Altium Designer ou logiciel EDA similaire

* Solide expérience en électronique, y compris la lecture et la compréhension de schémas électroniques, électronique numérique et analogique de base, intégration de capteurs, sélection de composants, fondamentaux de gestion de l'énergie, mise en service et validation matérielle
* À l'aise avec l'utilisation d'oscilloscopes, analyseurs logiques, multimètres et autres équipements de laboratoire
* Excellentes compétences en débogage et dépannage tant matériel que firmware

* Volonté de travailler étroitement avec une petite équipe de recherche pluridisciplinaire, et un fort intérêt pour la santé numérique et la neuro-réhabilitation
* Indépendance et esprit d'initiative, avec une attitude proactive et à l'aise pour développer et tester des idées novatrices
* Excellentes compétences en communication et relations interpersonnelles, avec un anglais écrit et parlé de premier ordre et de solides compétences en allemand.

* Expérience avec le développement Nordic nRF52/nRF54 ou STM32, Zephyr RTOS ou FreeRTOS, NFC ou USB, conception embarquée basse consommation serait un avantage
* Expérience avec des dispositifs médicaux ou portables alimentés par batterie
* Familiarité avec le développement et la réglementation des dispositifs médicaux, y compris ISO 13485, IEC 60601 ou normes connexes

Led by Prof. Dr. Thomas Zurbuchen, ETH Zurich | Space brings together space-related research, education and technology development across ETH Zurich. Working with academic, industrial and institutional partners, the initiative develops new space missions, instruments and technologies.
This position is offered as a fixed-term appointment for an initial period of two years, with the possibility of extension.
Projekthintergrund
The objective of this initiative is to establish and grow a centralized pool of space engineering expertise within ETH Zurich | Space. This pool supports ETH Zurich-led space projects and technology programs, strengthening ETH Zurich’s role in the Swiss and international space ecosystem.
The Flight Software Systems Engineer will support a diverse portfolio of small spacecraft, scientific instruments, robotic systems, and technology demonstrators. The work includes resource-constrained missions, integration with externally supplied spacecraft platforms, autonomous functions, and future distributed or coordinated spacecraft concepts.

This role interfaces across systems engineering, avionics, payloads, and software development, and coordinates with external platform providers and mission operations teams.
Aufgaben-/Stellenbeschreibung
As part of the specialized resource pool, you will provide flight software and software systems engineering expertise across multiple ETH Zurich space projects. You will contribute from early mission formulation and software architecture through implementation, integration, verification, launch preparation, and operations.

s.h: As part of your role, you will
s.t:
Take technical ownership of assigned flight software developments and act as the primary software interface to systems engineering, avionics, payload teams, mission operations, and external platform providers.
Translate mission concept of operations into spacecraft behaviors and define flight software architectures and functional decompositions
Allocate hardware-software functions, and define associated software requirements and interfaces.
Translate mission and system requirements into software specifications, interface control documents, operational concepts, and verification plans.
Develop embedded flight software in C and C++ and supporting tools and test scripts (e.g., Python), including device drivers, telemetry and telecommand handling, onboard data management, application software, and fault-management functions.
Integrate flight software with onboard computers, sensors, actuators, payload electronics, communication interfaces, ground systems, and externally supplied spacecraft platforms.
Set up and maintain flat-sat flight software testbeds
Perform software-related trade studies covering processing capacity, memory, timing, bandwidth, autonomy, reliability, and fault tolerance.
Develop real-time, event-driven, autonomous, synchronization, and GNC-related software functions where required.
Establish and maintain software baselines, configuration control, versioning, build automation, continuous integration, release management, and requirements traceability.
Develop and execute flight software unit tests, conduct integration, software-in-the-loop, processor-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and system-level verification and validation activities.
Support software risk management, anomaly investigation, non-conformance handling, and technical review boards.
Support spacecraft and payload assembly, integration, and test activities, commissioning, in-flight software updates, telemetry analysis, and mission operations.
Contribute to technical reviews, early-stage mission concepts, proposals, and software feasibility studies.
Provide technical guidance to junior engineers, researchers, and student teams.
Ihr Profil
You have a strong background in embedded and real-time software development combined with systems-level experience in software architecture, requirements engineering, interface definition, integration, and functional verification. You are comfortable working across mission, spacecraft, avionics, payload, software, and operations domains.

s.h: We are looking for someone with
s.t:
Master’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, computer engineering, aerospace engineering, robotics, or a related field.
5+ years of professional experience in flight software, embedded software, or mission-critical software systems.
Strong programming skills in C and C++ for resource-constrained embedded targets.
Experience with real-time operating systems, embedded Linux, or bare-metal development.
Experience in software systems engineering, including architecture definition, functional decomposition, hardware-software allocation, requirements management, and interface control.
Ability to translate mission and spacecraft requirements into software specifications, operational concepts, and verification strategies.
Experience integrating flight software with avionics hardware, sensors, actuators, communication buses, payloads, or ground systems.
Understanding of telemetry and telecommand, onboard data handling, timing, autonomy, fault management, and spacecraft operations.
Hands-on experience with software integration, debugging, automated testing, and hardware-in-the-loop environments.
Experience with configuration management, version control, release processes, technical baselines, and requirements traceability.
Ability to assess software-related technical resources, including processing capacity, memory, timing, bandwidth, and reliability margins.
Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
Knowledge of radiation effects, redundancy, memory protection, watchdogs, and FDIR.
Excellent command of English, both written and spoken; German is an advantage but not required.

s.h: Additionally, the following characteristics are a plus
s.t:
Experience developing flight software for CubeSats, small satellites, scientific instruments, planetary systems, or Class D/Gamma-type missions.
Experience leading or coordinating software-related and functional AIT activities, including test planning, execution, anomaly resolution, and system-level functional verification.
Experience integrating payload software with spacecraft platforms supplied by external industrial partners.
Familiarity with ECSS software engineering and software product assurance standards, NASA software practices, or comparable development frameworks.
Experience with spacecraft protocols and buses such as SpaceWire, CAN, UART, SPI, I²C, Ethernet, or CCSDS-based services.
Experience with flight software frameworks or operating systems such as NASA cFS, F Prime, RTEMS, FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or equivalent.
Experience with autonomous systems, robotic software, relative navigation, formation flying, or distributed spacecraft coordination.
Experience with FPGA or firmware interfaces and hardware-software co-design.
Experience with EGSE, simulators, ground software, commissioning, or in-orbit operations.
Experience collaborating with international partners, space agencies, research institutions, or spacecraft suppliers.
